flowchart TD
  Q[Queue for match]
  G[Create game]
  M[Exchange moves]
  E[End game]
  R[Update rating]
  Q --> G --> M --> E --> R

q: 峰值下悲观锁 claim 最先在哪里崩掉？
q_en: Under peak load, where does a pessimistic-lock claim break first?
scenario: 匹配池是一张共享 pending 表，峰值每秒几万次配对请求；多数玩家挤在中段 rating，同一小撮等待者同时是海量请求的候选人。团队用行级悲观锁（SELECT FOR UPDATE）保证一个人只被领走一次。
scenario_en: The matchmaking pool is one shared pending table taking tens of thousands of requests per second. Most players sit in a thick mid-rating band, so the same handful of waiters are candidates for huge numbers of requests at once. The team claims them with row-level pessimistic locks.
options: 所有 claim 在同一小撮热门等待者上串行排队，表被拖垮
锁只在数据库加了只读副本之后才生效，平时形同虚设
锁会让匹配质量下降，配到的对手 rating 差距被放大
锁把玩家的长轮询连接一并占住，客户端提前超时断开重连
options_en: Every claim serializes on the same few hot waiting players and the table grinds to a halt.
The lock only takes effect once read replicas are added; otherwise it does nothing.
Match quality drops because the rating gap to the paired opponent widens.
The lock also holds the long-poll connection, so clients time out and reconnect early.
optionExplanations: 对，热点行上的锁把并发请求排成一队，等待时间随并发线性增长，数据库先撑不住。
错，行级锁在单个数据库实例内就已生效并产生排队，与有没有副本无关。
错，配谁由 rating 窗口的查询条件决定，加锁只影响吞吐量，不改变配对结果。
错，长轮询握在接入节点上，数据库里的行锁不会占用那条 HTTP 请求。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a lock on a hot row queues concurrent claims, wait time grows linearly with concurrency, and the database gives out first.
Wrong — row locks already apply and already queue inside a single database instance; replicas are irrelevant.
Wrong — who you get paired with is decided by the rating-window query, not by locking; locking only caps throughput.
Wrong — the long poll is held by the front-end node; a database row lock does not occupy that HTTP request.
why: 中段 rating 密集让候选人集中在极少数行上，悲观锁把这些请求全部串行化；代价是吞吐塌到单行锁的速度，而且加索引救不了这种结构性竞争。
why_en: Mid-rating players cluster, so pessimistic locking serializes every claim onto the same few hot rows and throughput collapses to single-row lock speed — and no amount of indexing relieves that.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读取一行时就先加锁，其他事务必须等锁释放才能读改写同一行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pessimistic locking takes a lock as soon as a row is read, so other transactions must wait before they can modify it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 匹配 worker 把某个等待中的玩家标记为“归我了”的那次原子更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A claim is the atomic update in which one matchmaking worker takes ownership of a waiting player.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发出的请求被服务端一直挂着，直到有结果才返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Long polling means the server holds the client request open until a result is ready instead of replying immediately.

q: 改用乐观 CAS 抢人后，压力会转移成什么形态？
q_en: With optimistic compare-and-set claiming, what shape does the pressure take instead?
scenario: 同一个匹配池，改成乐观并发：worker 先读到候选等待者，再用 compare-and-set 更新其状态来抢人，抢不到就换下一个候选。中段 rating 依然是热点。
scenario_en: Same matchmaking pool, now optimistic: a worker reads a candidate waiter, then claims it with a compare-and-set on its status, and moves to the next candidate if it loses. The mid-rating band is still the hot spot.
options: 锁等待变成大量 CAS 失败重试，吞吐消耗在无效尝试上
抢人变成完全无竞争，热点问题就此被彻底消除
同一名玩家仍可能被两个 worker 同时配进两盘棋
数据库连接池会被长事务占满，因为每次 CAS 都要持有事务
options_en: Lock waiting turns into a flood of failed CAS retries, and throughput is spent on wasted attempts.
Claiming becomes contention-free, so the hot spot disappears entirely.
The same player can still be double-booked into two games by two workers.
The connection pool fills with long transactions, because every CAS holds one open.
optionExplanations: 对，抢输的 worker 立刻回头再试，热候选人上每成功一次都伴随一堆白跑的尝试。
错，竞争的源头是候选人集中在同一小撮人身上，换乐观只是把排队改成重来。
错，比较并交换保证只有一次更新能生效，双重配对正是它挡住的东西。
错，CAS 是一条短更新，不需要长事务；压垮系统的是重试次数而非事务时长。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a worker that loses immediately retries, so each success on a hot candidate comes with a pile of wasted attempts.
Wrong — the contention comes from candidates concentrating on a few people; going optimistic only swaps queueing for retrying.
Wrong — compare-and-set lets exactly one update land, which is precisely the double-booking it prevents.
Wrong — a CAS is one short update, not a long transaction; what overloads the system is retry volume, not transaction duration.
why: 热点是结构性的：乐观并发不排队但要重试，代价从等锁变成烧尝试次数，两条路都不是加索引能缓解的。
why_en: The contention here is structural: optimistic claiming does not queue but it does retry, so you burn attempts instead of waiting on locks — and indexing relieves neither.

termDefinitions.meaning: 比较并设置：只有当前值仍等于我读到的值时更新才生效，否则失败重来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-and-set means the update only lands if the current value still equals the value you read; otherwise it fails and you retry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不预先加锁，先做再在提交时检查有没有被别人改过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic concurrency takes no lock up front and instead checks at commit time whether someone else changed the data.

q: 把匹配池放在单 matcher 进程内存里，代价最先出现在哪？
q_en: If the pending pool lives in one matcher process’s memory, where does the cost show up first?
scenario: 有人提议把 pending 池放进单个 matcher 进程内存里的有序结构，按 rating 二分查找配对，读改写全在本地，没有网络跳也没有竞态。但峰值需要多个 matcher 实例，而且要能滚动发布。
scenario_en: One proposal keeps the pending pool in a sorted structure inside a single matcher process: binary-search by rating, pair locally, no network hop and no race. But peak load needs several matcher instances, and the service still has to be deployed.
options: 第二个实例视图分叉会双重配对，且进程崩溃丢掉整池排队者
有序结构上的二分查找在几万条等待者上会退化成全表扫描
本地读改写仍要跨进程加锁，延迟反而高于走一次网络的共享池
几万条等待请求放不进单机内存，必须先落盘再查找
options_en: A second instance forks the view and double-books players, and a crash drops the whole queue.
Binary search over tens of thousands of waiters degrades into a full scan.
Local read-modify-write still needs a cross-process lock, so it is slower than one network hop to a shared pool.
Tens of thousands of pending requests do not fit in one box’s memory and must be spilled to disk.
optionExplanations: 对，配对状态只活在一个堆里，多开一个实例两边都以为自己抢到人，重启则整队清零。
错，有序结构上的二分是 O(log n)，几万条也只有十几次比较。
错，同进程内配对本来就是纯本地操作，无需跨进程协调，这正是该方案唯一的长处。
错，几万条小记录只有几十 MB 量级，单机内存完全放得下。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the pairing state lives in one heap, so a second instance thinks it also won the player, and a restart wipes the queue.
Wrong — binary search on a sorted structure is O(log n); tens of thousands of entries take about a dozen comparisons.
Wrong — pairing inside one process is purely local with no cross-process coordination, which is the one thing this design gets right.
Wrong — tens of thousands of small records are tens of megabytes; memory is not the constraint.
why: 单进程方案买到的是无竞态的本地配对，代价是不能水平扩、崩溃即丢池、单点故障，所以池必须挪到所有 worker 都能读的共享存储。
why_en: A single process buys you race-free local pairing, but it cannot scale out, it loses the whole queue on a crash, and it is a single point of failure — so the pool has to move into a shared store.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读出当前值、按它算出新值、再写回去的这一组操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-modify-write reads the current value, computes a new one from it, and writes it back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个实例各自持有一份不同的“谁在等待”的状态，彼此看不到对方。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A forked view means two instances each hold their own version of who is waiting and cannot see each other’s.

q: 匹配池 Redis 的可用性该怎么加固？
q_en: How should we harden availability for the matchmaking pool in Redis?
scenario: pending 匹配池现在只在一个 Redis 主节点上，它是这条路径的单点。已知 pending 请求是短命的、客户端可以直接重新提交，而不是必须保住的对局状态。
scenario_en: The pending pool sits on one Redis primary and is a single point of failure. Pending match requests are cheap and ephemeral — clients can just re-submit them — not durable game state.
options: 把 pending 池双写进主数据库，Redis 只当只读缓存
跑副本并配自动故障转移，主挂了就提升一个副本
按 rating band 分片到多个 Redis，降低单点影响面
给每条 pending 请求开启 AOF 逐条落盘并强制同步刷盘
options_en: Dual-write the pending pool into the primary database and use Redis only as a read cache.
Run replicas with automatic failover and promote a replica if the primary dies.
Shard by rating band across several Redis nodes to shrink the blast radius.
Turn on AOF with a forced sync flush for every pending request.
optionExplanations: 错，双写把配对热路径又压回数据库，正是我们把池搬出来时要摆脱的东西。
对，秒级提升副本就恢复服务，切换中丢掉的少量在途请求由客户端重新提交补回。
错，分片是为了吞吐；某个分片挂掉时那一段 rating 的玩家照样配不上。
错，为短命数据逐条同步落盘要付出写放大，而且节点整体挂掉时它依然不可用。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — dual-writing pushes the matchmaking hot path back onto the database, exactly what moving the pool out was meant to avoid.
Correct — promoting a replica restores service in seconds, and the few in-flight requests lost in the cutover are simply re-submitted.
Wrong — sharding is a throughput tool; if one shard dies, players in that rating band still cannot get matched.
Wrong — per-request sync flushing pays write amplification for throwaway data and still leaves you down if the node itself dies.
why: pending 池是可重建的短命数据，可用性靠副本自动接管就够；代价是多维护一套复制与切换，而不是为它上昂贵的持久化。
why_en: The pending pool is cheap, rebuildable data, so replication with automatic failover is the right bar — the cost is running the replication and cutover machinery, not paying for durability.
tradeoff: 可用性（副本 + 自动故障转移） vs 持久性（为短命数据上同步落盘）
whenOtherWins: 如果池里存的是不可重建、客户端也无法重新提交的状态，就必须换成真正的持久化，而不只是副本切换。

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 自带的哨兵进程，监控主节点并在它失联时自动提升一个副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentinel is the Redis process that watches the primary and automatically promotes a replica when it stops responding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 追加写日志：把每条写命令按顺序追加到文件，用于重启后重建数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The append-only file records every write command in order so the dataset can be rebuilt after a restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点失效时把服务切换到另一个节点继续提供读写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover is switching service to another node when the primary fails.

q: worker 抢到这名等待者后，怎么把 gameId 送回他手里？
q_en: Once a worker wins the claim, how does the gameId reach that waiting player?
scenario: 玩家 POST 匹配请求后，由某台接入节点一直握着他的长轮询。稍后某个 matchmaker worker 用原子 claim 抢到了他——这个 worker 几乎肯定不是握着他连接的那个进程。
scenario_en: A player POSTs a match request and one front-end node holds their long poll open. Later some matchmaker worker wins the atomic claim on them — and that worker is almost certainly not the process holding their connection.
options: worker 直接向该玩家推 WebSocket 消息告知开局
发布到以 requestId 命名的 pub/sub 频道
写进数据库，让客户端退回每秒轮询 gameId 的做法
让每个接入节点定期扫描全表，自己找出被配对的请求
options_en: The worker pushes a WebSocket message straight to that player.
Publish on a pub/sub channel keyed by the requestId.
Write it to the database and have the client fall back to polling for a gameId.
Have every front-end node periodically scan the table for its own paired requests.
optionExplanations: 错，此刻对局 WebSocket 还没建立，worker 也不知道这名玩家挂在哪台节点上。
对，握着那条长轮询的节点订阅了这个频道，收到消息后就地完成挂起的请求并返回 gameId。
错，退回轮询把感知延迟拉到秒级，也白白浪费了已经握在手里的那条连接。
错，全表扫描让每个节点都承担全量读，配对越多越贵，延迟还由扫描周期决定。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — the gameplay WebSocket does not exist yet, and the worker has no idea which node holds this player.
Correct — the node holding that long poll is subscribed, so on receipt it completes the held request locally and returns the gameId.
Wrong — falling back to polling pushes perceived latency to seconds and wastes the connection you are already holding.
Wrong — full scans make every node read everything, get more expensive as pairings grow, and cap latency at the scan interval.
why: 配对的 worker 与握着长轮询的节点几乎总是不同进程，所以用 requestId 频道点对点唤醒那一个节点；代价是多依赖一层 pub/sub 投递。
why_en: The worker that pairs a player is almost never the process holding their held request, so we wake exactly that node through a channel keyed by requestId — at the cost of depending on pub/sub delivery.
tradeoff: pub/sub 定向唤醒 vs 客户端轮询 / 节点自行全表扫描
whenOtherWins: 如果匹配 worker 和握连接的节点就是同一个进程，直接在本地完成挂起的请求即可，不需要 pub/sub。

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布订阅：发送方往一个频道发消息，所有订阅该频道的进程收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In publish/subscribe a sender posts to a channel and every process subscribed to that channel receives it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次匹配请求的唯一标识，这里同时被当作唤醒频道的名字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The requestId uniquely identifies one match request and here doubles as the name of the wake-up channel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 配对成功后创建的那盘棋的标识，客户端拿它去开对局连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The gameId identifies the game created by a successful pairing; the client uses it to open the gameplay connection.

q: 什么条件成立时才该改成共享存储放 live state？
q_en: Under what condition should live game state move into a shared store?
scenario: 本设计把棋局 live state 留在 Game Server 内存里：单局几百字节、只活几分钟。共享存储那条路的好处很实在——任意服务器处理任意走子、路由不再是问题、服务器挂掉也不带走状态。
scenario_en: This design keeps live game state in the game server’s memory: a few hundred bytes per game, alive for a couple of minutes. The shared-store alternative has real upsides — any server handles any move, routing stops mattering, and a dying server takes nothing with it.
options: 当每局状态很大或生命周期很长，内存变贵时
当并发对局数超过十万、需要多台服务器时
当需要把走子历史持久化下来以便赛后复盘时
当团队希望省掉热路径上的那一次数据库写入时
options_en: When per-game state is large or long-lived enough that memory gets expensive.
When concurrent games pass a hundred thousand and need many servers.
When move history has to be persisted for post-game review.
When the team wants to drop that one database write from the hot path.
optionExplanations: 对，共享存储那次网络往返，只有在内存持有成本高到划不来时才值得换。
错，规模靠加机器和一致性哈希路由解决，跟状态放哪一层无关。
错，走子日志本来就在写，它服务恢复与复盘，并不要求 live state 外置。
错，那次写在 200ms 预算里只占几毫秒，换来的是崩溃后能重放。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the network round trip is only worth paying once holding the state in memory becomes the expensive option.
Wrong — scale is solved by more machines and consistent-hash routing, independent of where state lives.
Wrong — the move log is written anyway for recovery and review; it does not require externalizing live state.
Wrong — that write costs a few milliseconds out of a 200ms budget and buys replayable recovery.
why: 共享存储买到的是无状态服务器和免路由，代价是每一步一次网络往返；只有当 per-game 状态大或长命到内存变贵，这笔交易才划算。
why_en: A shared store buys stateless servers and no routing problem, at the price of a network round trip per move — a trade that only pays off once per-game state is big or long-lived enough to make memory expensive.
tradeoff: 内存持有（本地快、要路由） vs 共享存储（免路由、每步一跳）
whenOtherWins: 状态庞大且能跑上几天的回合制世界里，每步那一跳被摊薄，共享存储反而是更省心的一边。

termDefinitions.meaning: 对局进行中的活状态：棋盘局面、轮到谁走、双方剩余时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Live state is the in-progress state of a game: the board position, whose turn it is, and both clocks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把键映射到节点的方式，增删节点时只有一小部分键改变归属。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys to nodes so that adding or removing a node remaps only a small slice of keys.

q: 在无状态那条路线上，服务器崩溃会造成什么？
q_en: On the stateless route, what happens when one server crashes?
scenario: 假设我们走了另一条路：Game Server 完全无状态，棋盘、轮次、双方时钟都放在共享存储里，每步走子由任意一台服务器读出、校验、再写回。现在其中一台服务器进程崩溃。
scenario_en: Suppose we took the other route: game servers are fully stateless, and the board, turn, and both clocks live in a shared store, with any server loading, validating, and writing back each move. Now one of those server processes crashes.
options: 那台机器上的对局全部丢失，必须重放 move log 才能重建
对局不受影响，客户端重连到别的服务器即可继续
对局会卡住，直到那台服务器被拉起并重新加载状态
共享存储里的棋盘会回滚到崩溃前最后一次快照
options_en: Every game on that box is lost and has to be rebuilt by replaying the move log.
Games are unaffected; clients reconnect to another server and carry on.
Games stall until that server comes back and reloads its state.
The board in the shared store rolls back to the last snapshot before the crash.
optionExplanations: 错，那是内存持有方案才有的问题；无状态服务器身上没有独占的状态可丢。
对，状态本来就在共享存储里，任何一台服务器都能接手下一步，路由也不再是约束。
错，卡住的前提是状态绑在那台机器上，而这条路线里没有这种绑定。
错，新局面是逐步提交的，这里没有需要回滚的快照机制。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — that is the in-memory design’s failure mode; a stateless server holds nothing exclusive to lose.
Correct — the state already lives in the shared store, so any server can take the next move and routing stops constraining you.
Wrong — stalling requires the state to be pinned to that box, and nothing is pinned here.
Wrong — each new position is committed as it happens; there is no snapshot to roll back to.
why: 无状态加共享存储的真正收益是崩溃不带走状态、两名玩家也不必落在同一台机器上；代价是每一步都要付一读一写的网络往返。
why_en: The real upside of stateless servers over a shared store is that a crash takes no game with it and the two players need not land on the same box — paid for with a read and a write on every move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按顺序追加保存每一步走子的持久日志，用于重建棋盘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The move log is a durable append-only record of every move, used to rebuild the board.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不在本进程内存里保留请求之间的业务状态的服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stateless server keeps no business state in its own memory between requests.

q: 服务端该怎么保存并推进这两个棋钟？
q_en: How should the server store and advance the two chess clocks?
scenario: 50 万盘并发对局，服务端权威计时。棋钟只有在有人走子时才真正需要改变，而读取（推送给双方、算是否超时）随时可能发生。有人想给每盘棋起一个每秒 tick 的定时器。
scenario_en: Half a million concurrent games with a server-authoritative clock. A clock only truly changes when someone moves, but it can be read at any time. Someone proposes one per-game timer ticking every second.
options: 为每盘棋起一个每秒 tick 的定时器，把剩余时间写回存储
只存 remaining_ms 与启动时刻，读时现算
由客户端上报自己用掉的时间，服务端照记
把每次 ping/pong 量到的往返时间累加进剩余时间里
options_en: Run a per-game timer that ticks every second and writes the remaining time back.
Store remaining_ms plus the start timestamp and subtract elapsed time on read.
Let the client report how much time it used and record whatever it says.
Add each measured ping/pong round-trip straight onto the remaining time.
optionExplanations: 错，50 万个定时器意味着每秒 50 万次写，只为得到一个随时能算出来的数。
对，写入只发生在走子那一刻，其余时间剩余量都是读时用单调时钟现算出来的。
错，改过的客户端可以直接谎称自己从没掉过时间，权威值不能放在它那里。
错，往返时间是补偿返还的输入而不是余额，直接累加等于凭空送出时间。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — half a million timers means half a million writes per second just to maintain a number you can always compute.
Correct — writes happen only on a move; the rest of the time the remaining value is derived on read from a monotonic clock.
Wrong — a modified client can simply claim it never ran low; the authoritative value cannot live there.
Wrong — round-trip time is an input to latency credit, not a balance; adding it outright hands out free time.
why: 棋钟是可随时推导的值：剩余 = remaining_ms − (now − last_start)，其中 now 读单调时钟；代价是每次读都要算一次，换掉了 50 万个常驻定时器。
why_en: A clock is derivable on demand: remaining equals stored remaining_ms minus now minus last start, read off a monotonic clock — you pay a tiny computation per read instead of half a million live timers.
tradeoff: 读时按需计算（走子才写） vs 定时器 tick（持续写）
whenOtherWins: 如果剩余时间必须在无人走子时也主动触发外部动作，才需要额外挂一个到期定时器。

termDefinitions.meaning: 该玩家剩余的毫秒数，只在他走完一步时被重新写入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: remaining_ms is the player’s remaining milliseconds, rewritten only when they complete a move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只会向前走、不受系统时间被校准影响的时钟，用来量时间间隔。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A monotonic clock only moves forward and is unaffected by wall-clock adjustments, so it is what you measure intervals with.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从上次时钟启动到现在经过的时长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elapsed is how much time has passed since the clock last started.

q: 对局结束条件应该由哪部分逻辑产出？
q_en: Which piece of logic should produce the game-ending conditions?
scenario: Game Service 已经在每步走子时用内存棋盘校验合法性和轮次。产品还要处理将死、逼和/自动和棋、以及超时判负三种结束方式，团队在讨论要不要再引入一个独立规则引擎。
scenario_en: The game service already validates legality and turn order against the in-memory board on every move. The product also needs checkmate, stalemate and automatic draws, and flagging on time — and the team is debating a separate rules engine.
options: 由已有的走子校验逻辑顺带产出这三种结束
引入独立规则引擎，订阅 move log 后异步判定
由客户端检测到将死后上报，服务端确认
每步走子后额外查一次开局库和残局库来判定
options_en: Let the existing move-validation logic emit all three endings.
Add a separate rules engine that subscribes to the move log and decides asynchronously.
Have the client detect checkmate and report it for the server to confirm.
Consult an opening book and an endgame tablebase after each move.
optionExplanations: 对，校验一步是否合法时已经算出了对方的全部合法应招，没有应招就是将死或逼和。
错，异步判定会让一盘已经结束的棋还能收下一步，而且多一份规则实现要跟主路径对齐。
错，胜负和走子合法性一样是权威结果，交给客户端等于让它决定输赢。
错，开局库与残局库服务于赛后分析，跟当前局面是否已经终结无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — checking whether a move is legal already enumerates the opponent’s legal replies; no replies means checkmate or stalemate.
Wrong — deciding asynchronously lets a finished game accept another move, and it adds a second rules implementation to keep in step.
Wrong — the result is as authoritative as move legality; giving it to the client means letting the client decide who won.
Wrong — opening books and tablebases serve post-game analysis, not whether the current position is terminal.
why: 将死和逼和都是“没有合法应招”的两种情形，超时则由同一处扣时得出；代价只是校验函数要多返回一个结束原因，而不是多养一个系统。
why_en: Checkmate and stalemate are both just "no legal reply", and flagging falls out of the same clock deduction — the only cost is returning an end reason from the validator instead of running another system.
tradeoff: 复用走子校验 vs 独立规则引擎
whenOtherWins: 如果要支持大量可插拔的变体规则（不同棋种、自定义胜负条件），独立规则引擎才值得单开。

termDefinitions.meaning: 轮到走棋的一方没有任何合法着法但王没有被将，判和棋。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stalemate is when the side to move has no legal move but is not in check, so the game is a draw.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一方剩余时间归零，直接判其输棋。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flagging is losing because your remaining time hit zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先整理好的常见开局走法数据库，用于分析而非判定输赢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An opening book is a precomputed database of common opening lines, used for analysis rather than adjudication.

q: 在这个写入模式下，排行榜还需要额外的刷新机制吗？
q_en: Given this write pattern, does the leaderboard need any extra refresh mechanism?
scenario: 排行榜要求“对局结束后很快更新”。玩家的 rating 只会在一盘棋结束时被写一次，其余时间完全不变；有人担心榜单需要一个定期重算任务来保持新鲜。
scenario_en: The leaderboard must update shortly after games finish. A player’s rating is written exactly once, when a game ends, and never changes otherwise — yet someone worries the board needs a periodic recompute to stay fresh.
options: 需要，必须每分钟全量重算一次排名快照
不需要，写入只在赛后发生，更新完榜即最新
需要，因为 rating 会随时间衰减，榜会自然过期
需要，读多写少的榜必须靠定时预热才扛得住流量
options_en: Yes — recompute the whole ranking snapshot every minute.
No — writes only happen at game end, so the board is current the moment it updates.
Yes — ratings decay over time, so the board goes stale on its own.
Yes — a read-heavy board needs scheduled warming to survive the traffic.
optionExplanations: 错，全量重算是用来修复漂移的兜底手段，把它当主路径纯属浪费。
对，rating 变化和对局结束是同一个事件，写完就不存在落后的数据。
错，本设计里 ELO 只随比赛结果变动，没有随时间衰减这条规则。
错，预热解决的是读延迟，跟榜上数值是否过期是两码事。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — a full recompute is the backstop that repairs drift; using it as the main path is pure waste.
Correct — the rating change and the game ending are the same event, so nothing lags behind after the write.
Wrong — in this design ELO only moves with game results; there is no time-decay rule.
Wrong — warming addresses read latency, which is a different question from whether the values are stale.
why: 更新频率就等于对局结束频率，没有第三方写入源，所以新鲜度天然成立；真正要补的是幂等 apply 和定期对账，不是定时刷新。
why_en: The update rate is exactly the game-end rate and nothing else writes ratings, so freshness comes for free — what you actually owe is an idempotent apply and periodic reconciliation, not a refresh job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个随胜负升降的技能评分，赢强敌加得更多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ELO is a single skill rating that rises on wins and falls on losses, moving more when you beat a stronger player.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一个操作重复执行多次，结果和执行一次一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means applying the same operation repeatedly leaves the same result as applying it once.

q: 走子追加和时钟更新这两处写该怎么组织？
q_en: How should the move append and the clock update be organized as writes?
scenario: Game Server 失效转移后，新 owner 把 Game 行的 generation 从 N 抬到 N+1；被网络分区但仍活着的旧 owner 还在按 generation N 写。它每步要写两处：往 Moves 追加一条记录，以及更新 Game 行上双方的时钟。
scenario_en: After failover the new owner bumps the game row’s generation from N to N+1, while the partitioned-but-alive old owner still writes at generation N. Each move touches two things: an append to Moves and a clock update on the game row.
options: 两处写放在同一个事务里，共同受 generation 谓词保护
先追加 move，再单独更新时钟，各自失败就各自重试
只给时钟更新加 generation 判断，move 追加保持无条件
由新 owner 定期扫描并删除旧 generation 写进来的记录
options_en: Put both writes in one transaction guarded by the same generation predicate.
Append the move first, update the clock separately, and retry each on its own.
Guard only the clock update on generation and leave the move append unconditional.
Have the new owner periodically scan and delete records written at the old generation.
optionExplanations: 对，整个事务命中 generation <= :gen 才提交，僵尸服务器的两条写被一起静默丢弃。
错，分开重试会留下只落一半的中间态：棋步进了日志，时钟还停在上一手。
错，无条件追加会让僵尸写的走子混进日志，重放时棋盘就多出一步谁都没见过的棋。
错，事后清理既要能分辨哪些是脏数据，而且它被清掉之前已经能被重放读到。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the whole transaction commits only if it passes generation <= :gen, so the zombie’s two writes are dropped together and silently.
Wrong — retrying separately leaves a half-applied state: the move is in the log while the clock still reflects the previous one.
Wrong — an unconditional append lets zombie moves into the log, so replay rebuilds a board with a move neither player ever saw.
Wrong — cleaning up afterwards requires telling dirty rows apart, and they are already readable by replay before you get there.
why: fence 只有覆盖整组写才有意义：move 与时钟同事务、同谓词，要么一起生效要么一起被拒；代价是这一步必须走一次事务提交。
why_en: A fence only means anything if it covers the whole write set — move and clock in one transaction under one predicate, landing together or rejected together — which costs you a transaction commit per move.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 行上的一个计数器，每次这盘棋被重新分配 owner 就加一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The generation is a counter on the game row that is bumped every time the game is reassigned to a new owner.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写语句 WHERE 子句里的判断条件，不满足时这次写不生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A predicate is the condition in a write’s WHERE clause; if it is not satisfied, the write does not take effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 已经被替换、但仍在运行并试图继续写的旧 owner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A zombie server is an old owner that has been replaced yet is still running and trying to write.

q: 这个量级把恢复方案推向哪一边？
q_en: Which recovery design does this order of magnitude point to?
scenario: 一盘 40 步的棋，整条走子序列只有几百字节，重放一遍是微秒级；Game 行本身已经存着双方时钟和轮到谁走。团队在讨论要不要再加一张棋盘快照表来加快崩溃恢复。
scenario_en: A forty-move game is a few hundred bytes of moves and replays in microseconds, and the game row already carries both clocks and whose turn it is. The team is debating adding a board-snapshot table to speed up crash recovery.
options: 每 10 步存一次棋盘快照，缩短重放长度
不加快照，恢复就是读一行加重放几百字节
把整张棋盘每步写进 Game 行，省掉重放
为每盘棋在 Redis 里常驻一份棋盘副本兜底
options_en: Checkpoint the board every ten moves to shorten replay.
No snapshot — recovery is one row read plus replaying a few hundred bytes.
Write the whole board into the game row on every move so nothing is replayed.
Keep a standby copy of every board in Redis as a fallback.
optionExplanations: 错，checkpoint 是给长生命周期状态设计的，而 40 步的日志本来就短于一次快照。
对，读 Game 行拿到时钟与轮次，再顺序重放 move log 就还原了棋盘，几乎不耗时。
错，每步写整盘会把热路径的写放大几十倍，换来的只是省掉微秒级的重放。
错，多一份常驻副本就多一个会漂移的真相，还得为 50 万盘棋一直保持它是热的。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — checkpointing exists for long-lived state, and a forty-move log is already shorter than one snapshot.
Correct — read the game row for clocks and turn, replay the move log in order, and the board is back almost instantly.
Wrong — writing the full board every move amplifies hot-path writes many times over just to skip a microsecond replay.
Wrong — a standby copy is another truth that can drift, and you would keep it hot for half a million games.
why: 恢复数据量 = 走子步数 × 每步字节 ≈ 40 × 几字节 = 几百 Byte（字节），重放耗时以 μs（microsecond，微秒）计；这个量级直接判掉快照表。
why_en: Recovery size equals moves times bytes per move — about forty moves at a few bytes each, so a few hundred bytes replayed in microseconds, which is exactly why a snapshot table earns nothing here.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性把当前完整状态存一份，恢复时从它开始只重放之后的日志。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A checkpoint periodically stores the full current state so recovery only replays the log written after it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按顺序把日志里的每条操作重新执行一遍，得到当前状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay means re-applying every logged operation in order to reconstruct the current state.

q: 这套延迟补偿在单步上的准确性该怎么定位？
q_en: How accurate is this latency compensation on any single move?
scenario: 服务端按 median_rtt / 2 估一次单程传输，在扣时之前先返还给走子方，把 200ms 玩家每步约 170ms 的系统性损失抹掉大半。但 RTT 采样有抖动，去程和回程的路径也可能不对称。
scenario_en: The server estimates one-way transit as median RTT over two and credits it back before charging think time, erasing most of the roughly 170ms per move that a 200ms player was paying. But RTT samples are noisy and paths can be asymmetric.
options: 它是估计：单步可能偏差，但平均意义上公平
它是精确的，因为服务端时间戳是权威的
它精确到毫秒，因为取的是中位数而不是均值
它只在双方 RTT 相同时才成立，否则应该关闭
options_en: It is an estimate — off on any single move, fair on average.
It is exact, because the server timestamps are authoritative.
It is millisecond-exact, because it uses a median rather than a mean.
It only holds when both players have equal RTT; otherwise turn it off.
optionExplanations: 对，抖动加上路径不对称，单程并不等于往返的一半；补偿追求的是长期公平。
错，服务端时间戳只能证明消息何时到达，推不出它在路上走了多久。
错，中位数抗的是个别尖刺样本，并不能把一条不对称的路径变成对称。
错，RTT 不同正是要补偿的原因；关掉它等于把地理劣势原样留给远端玩家。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with jitter and asymmetric paths, one-way transit is not half the round trip; the goal is fairness over many moves.
Wrong — a server timestamp proves when a message arrived, not how long it spent in transit.
Wrong — a median suppresses outlier samples; it cannot make an asymmetric path symmetric.
Wrong — unequal RTT is the whole reason to compensate; switching it off just leaves the geographic penalty in place.
why: median_rtt / 2 是单程传输的估计量，噪声和非对称路径让它在任意一步上都不准；代价是接受统计意义上的公平，而不是逐步精确。
why_en: Half the median round-trip is an estimator for one-way transit, and noise plus path asymmetry make it wrong on any given move — you are buying fairness on average, not per-move precision.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返时延：一个包从客户端到服务端再回来所花的总时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-trip time is the total time for a packet to travel from client to server and back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把样本排序后取中间那个值，比均值更抗个别极端样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The median is the middle value of sorted samples and resists outliers better than the mean.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去程和回程走的网络路线不同，因而耗时不相等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Path asymmetry means the outbound and return routes differ, so they do not take equal time.

q: 本地倒计时与服务端权威时间的偏差该在哪一层处理？
q_en: Where should the gap between the local countdown and the authoritative clock be handled?
scenario: 客户端为了显示流畅在本地跑一份倒计时，服务端的权威剩余时间只在走子和 ack 时随消息下发。玩家因此会看到本地数字与刚收到的服务端数字短暂对不上。
scenario_en: The client runs a local countdown so the display is smooth, while the authoritative remaining time only arrives with move acks. So a player briefly sees the local number disagree with the number the server just sent.
options: 在 UI 层把显示平滑收敛到服务端下发的值
改协议，让服务端每 100ms 推一次权威时间
以客户端本地倒计时为准，服务端只做记录
偏差出现时暂停棋钟，等两边对齐再继续
options_en: Smooth the display toward the server’s value in the UI layer.
Change the protocol so the server pushes the authoritative time every 100ms.
Treat the local countdown as authoritative and have the server only record it.
Pause the clock whenever they disagree until the two sides line up.
optionExplanations: 对，权威值没错，错的只是两次下发之间的插值；把跳变做成渐进动画就够了。
错，为一个显示问题给 50 万盘棋加上常驻推送，把带宽花在没有信息量的消息上。
错，一旦以本地为准，改过的客户端就能声称自己从来不掉时间。
错，暂停是留给服务端故障的手段，用在正常的显示抖动上会被玩家当作拖延工具。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the authoritative value is fine; only the interpolation between pushes is off, so animate the correction instead.
Wrong — that adds a constant push stream across half a million games to fix a display issue, spending bandwidth on no information.
Wrong — once local is authoritative, a modified client can claim it never loses time.
Wrong — pausing is reserved for server failure; using it for normal display jitter hands players a stalling tool.
why: 本地倒计时只是两次权威下发之间的插值显示，差异应该在 UI 层平滑掉；代价是玩家偶尔会看到数字轻微跳一下。
why_en: The local countdown is just interpolation between authoritative updates, so the fix belongs in the UI — the price is that players occasionally see the number nudge.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端对一次走子的确认消息，其中带着权威的双方剩余时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the server’s confirmation of a move, carrying the authoritative remaining time for both sides.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在两次已知取值之间自己推算中间值，用来让显示连续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interpolation fills in values between two known data points so the display stays continuous.

q: 跨全库按局面聚合的查询应该落在哪种存储上？
q_en: Which store should archive-wide aggregation by position land on?
scenario: 已完成棋局永久保存，规模上百亿盘。要回答“这个局面下大家通常走什么”，需要跨全库按局面聚合，还要合并变位（不同走子顺序到达同一局面）。实时对局跑在 OLTP 库上。
scenario_en: Finished games are kept forever, on the order of ten billion. Answering "what do players usually play in this position" needs archive-wide aggregation by position, including transpositions. The live game runs on the OLTP database.
options: 就放在跑实时对局的 OLTP 库上，多加几个索引即可
列式或搜索存储，例如把棋局索引进 Elasticsearch
放进匹配池那套 Redis sorted set，用分数来排序
存成对象文件，每次查询临时起一批任务全量扫
options_en: Keep it on the OLTP database running live games and add a few indexes.
A columnar or search store — for example indexing games into Elasticsearch.
Put it in the same Redis sorted set as the matchmaking pool and sort by score.
Store object files and spin up a batch job to full-scan on every query.
optionExplanations: 错，把全库扫描型聚合压到实时库上，会直接吃掉走子路径的延迟预算。
对，按局面建立倒排或列存后只扫聚合列，变位也能归并到同一个局面键上。
错，sorted set 只能按单个分数排序，表达不了按局面维度的多字段聚合。
错，每次查询都全量扫上百亿盘既慢又贵，等于把索引工作推给每一次读。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — pushing archive-wide aggregation onto the live database eats straight into the move path’s latency budget.
Correct — an inverted or columnar index over positions scans only the aggregated fields, and transpositions collapse onto one position key.
Wrong — a sorted set orders by a single score and cannot express multi-field aggregation over positions.
Wrong — full-scanning ten billion games per query is slow and expensive; it pushes the indexing work onto every read.
why: 跨局面聚合是分析型全库扫描，跟实时对局的点写点读争同一份资源；代价是多养一套派生索引，并接受它比实时数据落后一段时间。
why_en: Aggregating across positions is an analytical full scan competing with the live game’s point reads and writes, so you run a separate derived index and accept that it lags the live data.
tradeoff: 分析型列式/搜索存储 vs 复用实时 OLTP 库
whenOtherWins: 如果只做按开局线路的查找，直接在走子序列上做前缀范围扫描就够，不必单独引入搜索存储。

termDefinitions.meaning: 联机事务处理：面向大量小事务、点读点写的数据库用法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online transaction processing describes a database serving many small point reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: transposition：不同的走子顺序最终到达同一个棋盘局面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transposition is when different move orders arrive at the same board position.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按列而不是按行组织数据，聚合时只读需要的那几列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A columnar store organizes data by column, so an aggregation reads only the columns it needs.
